newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader says time for action on budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader says time for action on budget.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Wednesday it was time for action on a balanced budget agreement between Congress and the White House but it was President Bill Clinton's turn to give some ground.

"I think its time for action. In every negotiation and every contract arrangement there comes a time when you have to enter the final agreement and move forward. I think that time is now," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said at a news conference.

Lott said, negotations among all parties would continue in hopes of reaching an accord that would balance the federal budget by 2002. "It is important that we face up to the needs for a balanced budget for the American people, some tax relief for working Americans, so that we get this job done," he said.

But in a warning to the White House, he added: "The president must come off of his continued insistence to spend more, more, more in many categories ... He also wants new entitlements. It takes give-and-take on both sides but I think it's his turn to give some."

Separately, White House Budget Director Franklin Raines expressed optimism to a Senate committee. "I hope that in the coming weeks, the administration can reach a bipartisan agreement with the Congress to put policies in place this year," Raines said.
Lott said a budget deal "must be real." He added: "It must get us to a balanced budget, it must have legitimate controls on the growth of entitlements."
